thread:
michal: Quick follow-up to the hotstart/weights-loading RFC — sorry for the long thread earlier, trying to distill a concrete proposal we can ship this quarter.

michal: Problem summary: current warmup API only supports "eager all" or "on-demand per-tensor", which forces either long tail cold starts for large sharded safetensors or unnecessary prefetch costs. We need a small orthogonal hint surface that lets callers express prioritization and granularity.

devon: Agree. The RFC had some ideas about manifests, but customers want fewer mandatory artifacts. How would this hint layer work with manifestless safetensors + shard index we already support?

michal: Proposal (sketch): expose WarmupHints on the loader interface. It's advisory only — runtime can ignore. Hints include: priority (int), tensor_ranges (list of (start,end) offsets or named ranges), and mode {"eager","lazy","kv-first"}. Example: 

```
WarmupHints {
  priority: 10,            // higher = earlier
  mode: "kv-first",      // prefer KV cache priming for chat workloads
  ranges: ["lm_head","wte", {"offset":0,"len":512}] // mix of names and byte ranges
}
```

lina: Love the kv-first mode. In practice most latency gains come from KV+position embeddings warming. Two questions: 1) can we make ranges optional and interpret empty as "use per-layer cost model"? 2) how to avoid leaking model-layout details to caller?

michal: Yes to (1) — empty ranges means runtime picks heuristics based on model topology + sequence length profile. For (2) we provide a small set of semantic range names ("kv","embed","lm_head","layer_n") and a lightweight manifest translator that maps semantic names to shard offsets when available. If no manifest, runtime uses index scanning to resolve names lazily.

ara: Tradeoff: index-scanning on first access adds small CPU/IO during hotstart. We should measure. Also want clear fallback to mmap for on-prem where streaming is expensive.

devon: Implementation note: make the hints part of the WeightSource v2 interface. Loader implementations (safetensors-stream, safetensors-mmap, tar-overlay) get WarmupHints but return a WarmupHandle future. That keeps the write path non-blocking.

prefetch-bot: perf/benchmark-suggested: run kv-first warmup vs eager-all on Llama-2-13B per-shard layout. Target metrics: 95p first-token-latency, cost-delta, and peak memory.

lina: Also add a safety cap on concurrent warmup IO per-host. We had noisy neighbors before. Suggest default cap = 3 per-GPU.

michal: Agreed. Next steps: 1) prototype WarmupHints plumbing in the loader interface (devon/ara), 2) add manifest-to-semantic-name translator + resolver (lina), 3) perf tests (prefetch-bot): run across mmap/streaming/zip backends. We'll iterate API shape after data.

devon: I'll open the PR for WeightSource v2 tomorrow. Will include a minimal test harness and a CLI flag to force semantic-name resolution to test manifestless flow.

michal: Thanks. If anyone is blocked by edgecases (shard-atomicity, partial-download failure modes), drop them here — we should decide whether warmup is best-effort or transactional. My bias: best-effort with clear metrics + fallback to smaller model variant on failure.

ara: Noted. I'll add a follow-up note on transactional vs best-effort and potential lease semantics for shard downloads.

michal: Great. Ping me in PR reviews. :thumbsup:
